entities.name: Iroas
entities.description: The god of victory, honor, and warfare on Theros, a centaur-like deity patron of Akros who stands for disciplined, honorable combat.

entities.name: Mogis
entities.description: Iroas's twin brother, who embodies carnage and brutality and revels in cruelty and senseless slaughter.

entities.name: Purphoros
entities.description: A god of Theros whose craftsmanship, especially of fine weapons, Iroas respects.

entities.name: Heliod
entities.description: A god of Theros who shares Iroas's belief in justice and order, though he can be arrogant and impulsive.

entities.name: Theros
entities.description: The plane where Iroas and the other gods dwell.

entities.name: Akros
entities.description: The polis of Theros of which Iroas is patron deity, closely tied to his civic and military ideals.

entities.name: Philomachos
entities.description: The shield borne on Iroas's left arm, with twin crescent notches.

entities.name: Iroan Games
entities.description: The greatest athletic contest in Theros, established by Iroas in Akros and held during the month of Iroagonion.

entities.name: Silence of the Gods
entities.description: A period during which Theros's deities were unable to directly intervene in mortal affairs.

events.summary: Iroas establishes the Iroan Games in Akros to celebrate courage and athletic excellence.
events.quote: He established the Iroan Games in Akros to celebrate these ideals

events.summary: The Silence of the Gods leaves Iroas and the other deities unable to intervene in mortal affairs, creating challenges for his worshippers.
events.quote: Iroas was affected by the Silence of the Gods

relations.note: Twin brothers whose enmity is intense and often violent.
relations.quote: Iroas is defined by his opposition to Mogis.
in contrast to his twin brother, Mogis

relations.note: They share a belief in justice and order; Iroas counsels restraint.
Iroas respects his craftsmanship but disapproves of his emotional instability.
relations.quote: Iroas respects Purphoros for his craftsmanship
He is revered as the patron deity of Akros
